title: When supplying manual context to an agent, can it get passed on to the LLM the agent creates?
body: I have a particular usecase where I manually supply the context to the agent I create. When I attach an LLM to it, that context is not passed down to it. Is that expected behavior?
author: Nicba1010

comments.body:
> I have a particular usecase where I manually supply the context to the agent I create. When I attach an LLM to it, that context is not passed down to it. Is that expected behavior?

@Nicba1010 can you share what you are referring to by "context"?
mcp_agent.context.Context to be precise. The thing that contains the config.

> mcp_agent.context.Context to be precise. The thing that contains the config.

Ah it does get passed down to the LLM as well. It's a mixin (see ContextDependent). You should be able to do LLM.context or self.context if you're extending the class.

If you share a code snippet I can help debug why that may not be happening.

```python
    # Create MCP Agent context
    mcp_agent_context: Context = create_mcp_agent_context(chat_session=chat_session)

    # Initialize MCP chat agent
    chat_agent: Agent = Agent(
        ...
        context=mcp_agent_context,
        ...
    )

    ...

    async def inner():
        async with chat_agent:
            llm: LLM = await chat_agent.attach_llm(OpenAIAugmentedLLM)
            llm._context = mcp_agent_contex

            response: str = await llm.generate_str(
                message=messages,
                request_params=RequestParams(
                    model=str(chat_session.llm_model.model),  # TODO: remove str cast
                    use_history=False,
                    maxTokens=16384
                )
            )
```

Without the `llm._context = mcp_agent_contex` it doesn't work. I might be doing something wrong though.
I think my main problem was running all this without an MCPApp, it works fine when using it. I'm closing the issue.

body:
I'm using the example code available on the README.md, I just made some changes to add new servers (todoist and brave-search).

_mcp_agents.config.yaml_
```yaml
mcp:
  servers:
    todoist:
      command: "npx"

    brave-search:
      command: "npx"
      args: ["@modelcontextprotocol/server-brave-search", "-y"]
    fetch:
      command: "uvx"
      args: ["mcp-server-fetch"]

openai:

```

_main.py_
```python
import asyncio

from mcp_agent.agents.agent import Agent
from mcp_agent.app import MCPApp
from mcp_agent.workflows.llm.augmented_llm_openai import OpenAIAugmentedLLM

app = MCPApp(name="mcp_basic_agent")


async def example_usage():
    async with app.run() as agent_app:
        logger = agent_app.logger
        personal_assistant = Agent(
            name="personal-assistant",
            instruction="""You are a personal assistant. You are able to help the user with their queries.""",
            server_names=["fetch", "todoist"],
        )

        async with personal_assistant:
            logger.info("personal-assistant: Connected to server, calling list_tools...")
            result = await personal_assistant.list_tools()
            logger.info("Tools available:", data=result.model_dump())

            llm = await personal_assistant.attach_llm(OpenAIAugmentedLLM)
            result = await llm.generate_str(
                message="Show my tasks due today",
            )
            logger.info(f"Result: {result}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import time

    start = time.time()
    asyncio.run(example_usage())
    end = time.time()
    t = end - start

    print(f"Total run time: {t:.2f}s")
```

title: Settings for MCPApp programmatically
body:
Hi, really like this project! :)

I have a use-case for programmatically defining settings when using the `MCPApp` class. E.g.:

```python
from mcp_agent.app import MCPApp
from mcp_agent.agents.agent import Agent
from mcp_agent.config import Settings, MCPSettings, MCPServerSettings, OpenAISettings
import asyncio

async def main():
    config = Settings(
            mcp=MCPSettings(
                servers={
                    "fetch": MCPServerSettings(
                        command="uvx",
                        args=["mcp-server-fetch"]
                    )
                }
            )
        )

    app = MCPApp(name="mcp_basic_agent", settings=config)
    
    async with app.run():
        agent = Agent(
            name="mcp_basic_agent",
            instruction="Test",
            server_names=["fetch"]
        )
        async with agent:
            # Raises error here: ValueError: Server 'fetch' not found in registry  
            print("Agent connected to server")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```
However, this raises an error when initializing the agent. This only works if there is a `mcp_agent.config.yaml` file with the following content: 
```yaml
mcp:
  servers:
    fetch:
      command: "uvx"
      args: ["mcp-server-fetch"]
```
I understand that this usage is not documented anywhere, however, according to the MCPApp interface this should be possible(?)
author: andersenthomas98

comments.body: @andersenthomas98 thanks for reaching out! this looks like a bug, as it should definitely be possible to set the settings object programmatically on MCPApp. I'll take a look soon
@andersenthomas98 this fix has been published to pypi in v0.0.8. Thank you for contributing the fix!

title: Progress Reporting Feature
body:
Draft of Progress Capture. 

Intent was to build on existing Logging System and provide a convenient way to produce rich display of progress events. Design should be simple to be able to add/filter scopes, add/easily enrich UX/progress display mechanisms and later use "Progress" log event types for high volume ephemeral comms.

Main changes:

 - File Logger saves in JSONL format
 - Secrets are obscured by the JSON serializer unless environment variable overrides
 - Addition of ProgressLogger which captures the log event stream to convert log events to progress info
 - Addition of contextual data to important log events for progress reporting
 - Rudimentary formatter for progress events (on by default, can be switched off with config option `progress_display=False`)
 - Offline summarizer, viewer, rich progress stimulator for further development and testing of display.

Future enhancements could include
 - Use of "Progress" log events specifically to capture ephemeral high volume status updates (e.g. token streaming, MCP notifications). 
 - Abstractions in the augmented_llm areas etc. to avoid duplication of intent. Better use of constants/common methods to allow identification of important progress events.
 - Console redirection and better use of Rich to make it more visually appealing.
 - Better display of intent (e.g. Agent Call vs. Assistant Call) for Chatting.
